name: Still Human // Wild
description: The spin-off of Still Human, with the walls taken off. One hundred and ninety metres of hand-pressed clay country — plains, a river cut, a ridge line with snow on it — and a kiln at the middle of it that nothing can break. Look at a tree, a boulder or a clay bank and hold the button: a ring fills and it comes up in one piece. Craft an axe and a pick at the bench and it comes up faster and gives more. Sculpt the hill into a shape you meant, raise a house out of brick, thatch, timber, cut stone, kiln glass and lantern light. After dark the ground gives up husks, stalkers, lumberers, emberwisps and molders, and every single one of them leaves a weapon or a piece of plate on the grass before it goes; dawn burns whatever is still standing. Spend what you gather on the kiln itself — widen the protected ring, feed the braziers, raise the tower, better the bench — and the safe ground grows with you. Third person over the shoulder, stop-motion at twelve frames a second, and the world you changed is still changed when you come back.

inputs.description: The resident — read from the shell so the ground is filed under the same name you use everywhere else in the hub.

outputs.description: The ground itself — seed, day count, every cell of terrain you raised or lowered, every block you placed, which trees, boulders and clay banks are gone, the kiln's upgrade levels, your tools, your kit and what is spare. Written on leaving and every twenty-two seconds, so a run survives the window closing.

author: Present Palm
